digest.component_or_area: plan-review criterion T1 (overlay-prior-art) and web search capability gating
propositions: The Bedrock cutover removed server-side web search from blocking criterion T1 silently because the provider-name prefix gate `resolved.startswith('anthropic')` fails for bedrock-qualified Claude models, causing T1 to ground claims in codebase knowledge instead of current web sources.

Web-search capability gating by provider-name prefix violates the epic's zero-exceptions rule that provider qualification must derive from registry membership, not prefix shape, and this violation became visible only when the same model (Claude) reached through a different provider name lost its capability.

The failure is silent: no warning is logged and the signed verdict's `provider_provenance.capabilities` does not record that web search was withheld, making the degradation in T1's decision quality unobservable in the verdict.

The operator requirement is that T1 must have web access on every provider rebar can route it to, regardless of whether the provider offers a native server-side tool, necessitating a rebar-side mechanism where providers lack native support.

The decision to attach web search must be relocated from anthropic_model.py and made independent of both model string and provider name, deriving instead from the model profile's capability registry via `supported_native_tools` membership.
The provider_provenance.capabilities payload must record web_access as 'native'|'local'|'off' to make future silent withdrawals observable and prevent regression.
